newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares surge to fresh record high in bourse.
newsitem.headline: German shares surge to fresh record high in bourse.

text.p: Germany's DAX index surged to a fresh record high in early bourse dealings on Thursday as the blue-chip index set its sights on breaking 4,000 points in the coming weeks with fresh energy from the stronger dollar.

The 30-share DAX index was up 26.07 points at 3,880.83 points after reaching a new all-time high at 3,892.30 points. The IBIS DAX, which reflects all-day computer dealings, was up 12.06 points at 3,879.59 points.

Traders said profit-taking may set in ahead of the release at 1230 GMT of U.S. jobless data for May as the German market waits for the report's impact on U.S. financial markets ahead of the Independence Day long holiday weekend.
"The market is well-bid and the DAX could very well reach 3,900 today," said one Frankfurt trader. "But investors are going to be cautious, so I expect some more consolidation."
Overnight Wall Street gains, where the Dow Jones index surged about one percent to 7,795.38 points, and the dollar trading above 1.75 marks were the main factors driving the DAX.
The higher dollar was underpinning export-sensitive shares, particularly in the chemical and automotive sectors, as traders said the DAX could break 4,000 points in the next few weeks.
"The ace in the pack is how the U.S. jobs data comes out today," said a Frankfurt share trader.
"The problem, however, is that the market is in blue skies, so it is hard to say where the gains should stop. We could see 4,000 points fairly soon," the trader said.

Chemical shares, which were at the market forefront earlier in the week, were generally lower on profit-taking following recent sharp gains. But traders said the sector was still in vogue and that the uptrend would resume in the near-term.
Hoechst AG, which has risen more than 10 percent since June 25, was down 1.20 marks to 78.10 marks.
But Bayer AG was up 63 pfennigs at 71.38 marks and BASF AG was up 10 pfennigs at 66.15 marks.
Bank shares were mixed as Deutche Bank AG slipped 45 pfennigs to 104.35 marks after setting another new record high at 105.35 marks in IBIS dealings.
Daimler-Benz AG was up 50 pfennigs at 145.40 marks after also setting a new record high at 146.20 marks in IBIS.
Other carmakers were higher, including Volkswagen AG rising 45 marks to 1,390 marks and BMW AG gaining 15 marks to 1,457 marks.
Porsche, another top gainer in recent weeks, was up 110 marks at 2,620 marks. Brokerage house Lehman said this week it set a price target for Porsche at 3,600 marks.
